item.title: I Built a PC Monitor That Learns Your Hardware
item.content:encoded:
Every traditional PC monitor — Afterburner, HWiNFO, CCleaner, GeForce Experience — runs on absolute thresholds and general profiles. "If temp over 80, alert." But your machine isn't in any table: silicon lottery, component aging, ambient temperature, and load composition mean a generic profile describes a computer you don't own. The fix is statistics on YOUR history, not the manufacturer's spec — median + MAD with Nelson Rules (the same Statistical Process Control factories use), workload-bucketed thermal baselines via Welford's algorithm, all running locally and offline with zero telemetry. A PSU rail sagging to 11.7V is "in spec" to a threshold but a 5-sigma anomaly against your own learned 11.95-12.05V norm — caught months before failure. Not a chatbot bolted on. Real statistics that don't hallucinate. It's working open-source code in PC Workman v1.7.9, built solo over 11 months between physical-labor shifts.
